relationships.x_label: Crude oil price, US$ (% change on a year)
relationships.why: Oil feeds into fuel, transport and input costs.
relationships.caution: PPAC publishes no monthly crude prices for 2022-23, so this rests on the months since then only.

relationships.x_label: Rupee depreciation against the US$ (% on a year)
relationships.why: A weaker rupee makes imports, including oil, dearer in rupees.

relationships.x_label: Repo rate (change on a year, points)
relationships.y_label: Non-food bank credit growth (% a year)
relationships.why: Higher policy rates should, with a delay, slow bank lending.
relationships.caution: The link here is positive: RBI raised rates in 2022-24 just as lending recovered strongly after COVID. Both followed the same cycle; this does not mean that rate rises increase lending.

relationships.x_label: Repo rate (change on a year, points)
relationships.why: Monetary policy is meant to act on inflation with a delay.
relationships.caution: RBI also sets the repo rate in response to inflation, so the two move in both directions at once; a simple correlation cannot separate them.

relationships.y_label: Households' expected inflation, a year ahead (%)
relationships.why: Do households' expectations follow the inflation they have seen?
relationships.caution: Expectations are surveyed every two months, so this uses those months only.

relationships.why: Bond investors ask for higher yields when inflation rises.

relationships.x_label: Merchandise imports, 3 months (% on a year)
relationships.y_label: Merchandise exports, 3 months (% on a year)
relationships.why: Much of what India exports uses imported inputs.
relationships.caution: Both also rise and fall with world prices, especially of oil, which India imports, refines and re-exports.

relationships.why: Portfolio outflows tend to weaken the rupee.

relationships.x_label: Non-food bank credit growth (% a year)
relationships.y_label: Gross GST, 3 months (% on a year)
relationships.why: Faster lending and faster spending tend to go together.
